top_categories.workout_context: 22,309ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
166 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Alpenbrevet's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
At Alpenbrevet, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 166 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
22,309ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
134ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Alpenbrevet. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 166 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Alpenbrevet. Train it until it feels boring.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 22,309ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
166 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Low-cadence force work supports 22,309ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: September in Andermatt, Switzerland. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Alpenbrevet. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 166 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 166 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.altitude: Alpenbrevet includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Durability, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 166 miles of mixed terrain in Andermatt, Switzerland.
